claim: Mean yield differs substantially by crop in the validated 10,000-row dataset; Sugarcane has the highest mean and Cotton the lowest among the six crop groups.
supporting_result: Crop means range from 7.4279 t/ha (Cotton) to 74.8303 t/ha (Sugarcane).
uncertainty: Group standard deviations are reported in A002; this is descriptive and no causal interpretation is made.
limitations: Static dataset; provenance and units remain unresolved; group differences may reflect data-generation structure.

claim: Fertiliser use has a moderate positive within-crop Pearson association with yield across all six crops.
supporting_result: Crop-specific r values range from 0.4928 (Potato) to 0.5346 (Maize), with n from 1,633 to 1,702.
uncertainty: Pearson correlations and p-values are deterministic outputs; confidence intervals were not part of these baseline results.
limitations: Association is not causation; linear association may not capture nonlinear structure; multiple related tests and dataset provenance require review.

claim: Rainfall has a moderate positive within-crop Pearson association with yield, while the pooled rainfall association is much weaker.
supporting_result: Crop-specific r values range from 0.4356 to 0.4751; pooled A016 reports r=0.0312, illustrating aggregation attenuation.
limitations: Aggregation effects, confounding, static data, and unresolved provenance limit interpretation.

claim: The reproduced crop-specific irrigation ANOVA tests do not provide evidence of statistically significant yield differences among irrigation categories at the unadjusted 0.05 level.
supporting_result: p-values range from 0.1051 to 0.8722 across the six crop analyses.
uncertainty: Baseline classical ANOVA assumptions and multiple-testing controls were reviewed separately; this is not evidence that irrigation has no effect.
limitations: Non-significance does not establish equivalence; unequal-variance alternatives may be appropriate under D014.

claim: The reproduced crop-specific OLS specifications have adjusted R² values between approximately 56% and 62%; coefficient-level interpretations are withheld pending resolution of the Cotton specification concern under D017.
supporting_result: Adjusted R² ranges from 0.5615 (Wheat) to 0.6138 (Maize); exact covariates are listed in the Analysis Register and original regression summaries are preserved.
uncertainty: HC3 inference and multiple-testing implications require explicit review before coefficient interpretation.
limitations: No coefficient direction is promoted as a finding until the Cotton RESET/specification issue is resolved; no causal claims.

claim: On the fixed holdout, gradient boosting performs better than both the global-mean and training-only crop-mean benchmarks, while linear regression and Random Forest are also compared against those baselines.
supporting_result: Global-mean and crop-mean benchmark metrics, plus linear, Random Forest and gradient boosting metrics, are recorded in model_metrics.csv.
uncertainty: Five-fold training cross-validation and one fixed holdout use seed 20261011; independently supplied split-seed sensitivity is not reproduced here unless separately documented.
limitations: Very high performance may reflect unknown data-generation structure; no real-world generalisation claim is made while provenance remains unknown.

claim: Random Forest holdout permutation importance identifies Crop_Type as the largest predictive contributor, followed by Fertilizer_Used and Rainfall.
supporting_result: Permutation importance means: Crop_Type 32.5964, Fertilizer_Used 0.4828, Rainfall 0.3506, Soil_Moisture 0.1275.
uncertainty: Importance uses 10 holdout permutations under the fixed model and seed.
limitations: Predictive contribution is not causal importance; correlated predictors and crop encoding can affect rankings.
